text:
sre-bot: INCIDENT detected — hosted-api request queue p95/p99 spike in us-west-2. Queue growth observed at 11:03 PDT, GPU pool saturation (gputype-a) and autoscaler failing to provision new nodes. Severity: P1. Pager sent to #oncall.

oncall_jay: Ack'd. I'm on it. Seeing elevated 95/99 latencies, errors rising. Any quick context? Is this client-driven (big customer) or platform-wide?

cheng: From metrics: sudden traffic burst from multiple API keys starting ~11:01. request_queue_length climbed from 50 -> 420 in ~3m. GPU utilization pinned at 98-100%. p95 jumped to 1.6s then p99 -> 6.1s and timeouts increasing. No obvious deploy at 10:50. Adding graphs: (metrics-bot attached)

metrics-bot: Graph links: https://metrics/redwood/hosted-api/us-west-2/queue_length?from=11:00&to=11:10

tara: Trying a provisioner check now. Running: `infractl pools list --region us-west-2 --type gputype-a`

tara: provisioner responds but new instance create attempts failing with: `ProvisionError: QuotaExceeded: Insufficient GPUs for region` — cloud quotas look exhausted in this account/region.

alex: Confirmed quota errors in provisioner logs: ```[11:05:12] provisioner: create_instance failed: ApiError(403, 'QuotaExceeded')
[11:05:13] autoscaler: scale_loop failed, retrying
[11:05:19] autoscaler: still at desired=0 pending_creates=3 failed_creates=3``` 

oncall_jay: So autoscaler is looping but unable to create capacity. We need mitigations: (1) rate-limit noisy keys, (2) fallback routing to dedicated pools or smaller models, (3) manual quota request/override if possible. Who can run quick key throttles?

support_lead: I can coordinate throttling for specific API keys. Cheng, do you have top offending keys list? We should message affected customers ASAP if they hit their SLA.

cheng: Top 5 API keys by qps: key-A (50% of burst), key-B (20%), then several small ones. Suggest immediate temporary quota on key-A to 50% of current to stabilize.

tara: Applying key-level throttles now: `redwoodctl rate-limit set --key key-A --rps 20 --duration 15m` — applied. Also enabling degraded fallback routing: prefer-compact-models for non-enterprise routes.

sre-bot: ACTION: key-A throttled by oncall_jay. Fallback routing enabled for route=/v1/generate for non-e2e customers.

alex: After throttling, queue dropped from 420 -> 180 in ~4m, p95 improved to ~900ms, p99 down to ~2.3s. Still above SLO but better. We need longer-term capacity or to free up quota.

infra-bot: Quick note: there's a pending spot capacity in us-west-2 but our cloud quota restricts GPU SKU creations. If we shift some workloads to us-east-1 temporarily we could relieve pressure.

cheng: Can we reroute low-priority traffic (batch/embeddings) from us-west-2 -> us-east-1? That would free GPU slots. Need approval to touch routing rules.

oncall_jay: Do it. Prioritize realtime hosted-api traffic for paid customers in us-west-2. Move embeddings/batch to us-east-1. Tara, can you change the policy?

tara: Updating routing policy: `rbacctl route update --filter 'workload:batch OR workload:embedding' --target-region us-east-1` — applying. Will take ~60s to propagate.

tara: Propagation done. Metrics show embeddings QPS in us-west-2 dropping 85% and bumping up in us-east-1. Queue in us-west-2 now ~60, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s.

support_lead: Support notified top affected customers. Messages drafted for status page and targeted DMs. ETA for final fix depends on cloud quota increase or manual pool creation in another account.

alex: We're still seeing autoscaler failed_creates due to quota. I'll open an emergency quota request with cloud console and also request permission to borrow from our backup account to create a manual pool.

oncall_jay: Good. Documenting customer impact: approx 11:01-11:15 elevated latencies and transient timeouts for some requests. No confirmed data loss; retries succeeded for most. Logged customers impacted: corpA, corpB, corpC (partial). Support will escalate any customer severity.

cheng: Pushing a temporary fallback: enable model-quantized small profile for hosted-api for non-enterprise keys (reduces GPU mem/latency). Patch applied. Observed token throughput increase and lower memory pressure.

metrics-bot: After changes (throttle + reroute + quantized fallback) at 11:12: p95 -> 320ms, p99 -> 800ms, queue ~25. Error rate back to baseline in 11:14.

sre-bot: INCIDENT state: Mitigated. Postmortem required. Assigning to cheng (owner) and alex (infra follow-up). Please capture root cause: (a) burst traffic pattern allowing single key to dominate, (b) regional GPU quota exhaustion, (c) autoscaler lacks graceful degraded path when create APIs fail.

support_lead: I'll send a short customer-facing summary to affected accounts and update status page: "Mitigated — performance restored, investigating root cause."

oncall_jay: Handoff: I'm handing on-call to cheng for next shift remediation and postmortem. cheng, please take over and update ops-runbook with steps we did (throttle, reroute, quantize). I am available if escalation needed.

cheng: Taking on-call. I'll coordinate with alex to get quota increase and schedule a runbook update + prioritized engineering fix for autoscaler retry/backoff handling. ETA for postmortem draft: today EOD.

alex: Filed cloud quota ticket #Q-43219 and requested emergency increase. Also opening infra task to enable cross-region burst drains as a permanent mitigation. Created ticket: INFRA-2983.

tara: Logging commands and snippets used during incident in case doc: ```
redwoodctl rate-limit set --key key-A --rps 20 --duration 15m
rbacctl route update --filter 'workload:batch OR workload:embedding' --target-region us-east-1
redwoodctl feature-toggle set hosted-api.quantized-fallback true --scope non-enterprise
``` 

sre-bot: Closing notes: No customer data compromised. Recommend follow-ups: improve autoscaler error classification, add proactive quota monitor per region, and customer-facing metrics on rate limit actions. Marking incident as mitigated at 11:15 PDT.
